newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan growers warn of African coffee shipment.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan growers warn of African coffee shipment.

text.p: Nicaragua's coffee growers on Wednesday warned that a shipment of coffee from Africa, possibly carrying the coffee berry disease (CBD), was on route to Nicaragua and called for it to be turned back.

"We know that a shipment of African coffee is on its way, imported by a Nicaraguan company, endangering not only the Nicaraguan harvest, but Central America's and Mexico's as well," the co-president of the Nicarguan Union of Coffee Growers (Unicafe), Amilcar Navarro, told a news conference.

Navarro called on authorities to turn back the 10,000- quintal (100-lb bag) shipment of robusta coffee or to burn it immediately once it arrives to stop all chance of any infected beans from the disease infesting Nicaraguan coffee crops.
CBD is caused by a fungi whose scientific name is collethotrichum kahawac.

He did not say on what day it was expected to arrive. Officials also said they did not know which port in the African continent they beans were coming from. They made no mention of a specific country.

"The Nicaraguan government has received a concerned message from other coffee institutions in Central America and the region about the possibility that a Nicaraguan business is importing robusta coffee from Africa," he said.
Latin America currently has no incidence of CBD, which affects African crops, and regional countries have strictly enforced laws prohibiting the importation of coffee from Africa, Navarro said.
CBD affects exclusively Arabica coffee (Cafe Arabica) plantations, but he said the disease could be introduced via Robusta beans.
The disease attacks the green beans when they are already formed, preventing them from maturing and causing losses of up to 80 percent of production, he said.
The Nicaraguan company importing the African coffee was CISA S.A., makers of soluble coffee, he said.
